The old observatory had been closed for decades, but every Thursday at precisely 11:17 PM, the telescope dome still rotated a few inches toward the eastern sky. Nobody could explain it. The caretaker insisted the machinery had been disconnected in 1984, yet the dome continued its patient little movement year after year, as though something above the rooftops were quietly asking to be noticed.

Meanwhile, somewhere beneath a city that had forgotten how to grow gardens, a tiny green shoot pushed its way through a crack in the concrete. It had no knowledge of traffic, politics, deadlines, or human ambition. It simply followed the light. By morning, someone had placed a coffee cup beside it, perhaps as a joke, perhaps as an offering, and for one strangely peaceful moment the entire sidewalk seemed to belong to both of them.
